classification.difficultyReason: Read the starting probability and recognise that adding favourable cards changes both numerator and denominator.

inlines.text: The probability of choosing a card less than 3 is shown on the scale.
How many more cards less than 3 do you need to add so that the probability of getting a number less than 3 is 0.5? Show all your working.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 23, between the introductory sentences and the final instruction
spec.description: A horizontal scale with 11 equally spaced ticks and an orange downward marker at the fourth tick from the left. Endpoint labels 0 and 1 implement approved correction p16-source-corrections.
spec.mathematics: Ten equal intervals span 0 to 1. The marker is three intervals from 0, at probability 0.3. Intermediate ticks remain unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The base scale, marker and approved endpoint labels are student-visible. No 0.3 label, card count or solution annotation is printed.

answer.worked:
The scale shows a probability of $0.3$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Cards less than 3}&=0.3\times20\\\text{Cards less than 3}&=6\end{align*}$$

The initial probability is $\frac{6}{20}$. Let $x$ be the number of cards less than 3 added.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{6+x}{20+x}&=\frac{1}{2}\\2(6+x)&=20+x\\12+2x&=20+x\\x&=8\end{align*}$$

Add 8 cards.

Check:
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{6+8}{20+8}\\P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{14}{28}\\P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
